justifications.durability: The test now fails if the fixture regresses: reinstating the bare 999999 (the node's own negative control, logs/negative_control.txt, EXIT=1) reddens test_shot_without_cache_refuses_and_names_the_cache with the pulse-token refusal, and the companion assertions on 'no EDDB cache' and JT60SA_ROOT / '999999.zarr' are independent of the token the test passes in, so the test guards that a lettered pulse reaches the cache branch rather than echoing its input.

One point off: only one of the two named tests required work.
justifications.reuse: No new capability is added: the change reuses the existing write_pulse entry point and the module's production eddb_token refusal rather than forking a guard, and the search over tests/data found the pulse-naming idiom already owned by the test itself.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every changed line is inside the declared path tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py; no engine source, plan, index or figure touched and the worktree is clean, so the diff carries nothing the goal does not imply.

raw_text:
Independent review of run r-20261008T031233296799-jtfm-pulse-writer-test-tokens (plan imas-ambix:jt60sa-facility-mint section 16), head 5152672e9162561420f543a8b5c1ac73044b8267 on base f18db7f17cf6ff30fd461421691a4923e0b46e56.

The node repairs a test that the section-16 refusal change turned misleading. Section 16 makes write_pulse
resolve the pulse through eddb_token before any fetch, so a token with no series letter is refused with the
pulse-token error instead of the late cache error. The old test tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py::
test_shot_without_cache_refuses_and_names_the_cache called write_pulse(MACHINE, 999999, tmp_path) and asserted
the 'no EDDB cache' branch, so it hit the pulse-token refusal instead and failed at base. The node changes the
call to write_pulse(MACHINE, 'E999999', tmp_path) and the message assertion from '999999' to 'E999999', leaving
the companion assertions on 'no EDDB cache' and on the integer cache directory JT60SA_ROOT / '999999.zarr' in place.

DIFF. One commit, 5152672e9162561420f543a8b5c1ac73044b8267, on base f18db7f17cf6ff30fd461421691a4923e0b46e56; a single path, tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py, +2/-2.
No engine source touched. git status of the reviewed worktree is clean at 5152672e9162561420f543a8b5c1ac73044b8267. Local-transport
tests/data/test_eddb_local_transport.py already names its pulse with the full token (PF_ACTIVE_SHOT E101154) and
passes at base, so the node correctly left it unchanged, as the done-when directs.

REPRODUCTION AND GATE. I ran the single target test at the reviewed head in the reviewed worktree:
pytest tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py::test_shot_without_cache_refuses_and_names_the_cache -> 1 passed, EXIT=0.
The reviewed run's own arms: base.txt (base f18db7f17cf6ff30fd461421691a4923e0b46e56) is 2 failed / 8 passed, EXIT=1, failing ids
test_write_covers_every_description_ids_in_one_file and test_shot_without_cache_refuses_and_names_the_cache; the head
arm is 1 failed / 9 passed (target test PASSED), the survivor being the pre-existing
test_write_covers_every_description_ids_in_one_file, which fails at base too. Both files add no failures.
ruff check imas_ambix tests packages -> All checks passed, EXIT=0 (I reproduced it, --no-cache).

NEGATIVE CONTROL. Declared string: putting 999999 back as a bare number makes the target test fail with the
pulse-token refusal instead of the cache refusal. The log at logs/negative_control.txt shows EXIT=1 and the
failing id tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py::test_shot_without_cache_refuses_and_names_the_cache raising
imas_alambic.eddb.EddbCacheError: 999999 is not an EDDB pulse token. The head arm does not fail that id, so the
control is admitted.

FINDING. The head arm the manifest names is not readable from the artefact it cites. after_suite names
logs/head.txt with completed true, failure_count 1; the stored head.txt is 14 lines and 1435 bytes, ending at
'tests/data/test_pulse_writer.py F.......' with no summary line and no EXIT= (pytest -rA prints the per-item
lines then a one-line summary, as the complete base.txt does). The run's stderr and transcript show the worker
re-ran the head arm several times and the final re-run was killed by srun ('srun: forcing job termination',
'Killed', CANCELLED 2026-10-08T05:36:56 local = 03:36:59Z, the run's own deadline), overwriting the earlier
complete run (visible in the transcript as '1 failed, 9 passed in 29.06s' style summary). So the claimed figure is
real but the named artefact cannot confirm it. My own re-run of the target test, and the head failing id recovered
from the transcript, both corroborate the claim, so this does not hold the node.

BEFORE/AFTER. Before: the missing-cache test called write_pulse with bare 999999 and, after section 16 added the
token refusal, failed on the pulse-token error, naming the wrong cause. After: it calls write_pulse with
'E999999'; the pulse is named by its full EDDB token, the refusal reaches the asserted 'no EDDB cache' branch,
and the message still carries the integer cache directory JT60SA_ROOT / '999999.zarr' (the directory name keeps
accepting bare digits). One test moved from failing to passing with no test added or lost.
